name: Maunga Terevaka from Ahu Akivi
region: Rapa Nui National Park, Easter Island
why: Up the grass slopes from the seven moai of Ahu Akivi to the island's highest point, where the whole of Rapa Nui and the round Pacific horizon are in one view.
book: Rapa Nui National Park ticket and an accredited Ma'u Henua guide, required for park visits (Ahu Akivi is a guarded site). Terevaka is a recovery area: on foot or on horseback only, no vehicles.
water: None on the way: carry 1.5-2 litres.
dangers: No shade and strong wind on the open summit.
The path fades higher up: in cloud keep to the ridge and go back the way you came.
Cattle and horses graze the slopes; close the gates.
turnaround: In cloud or rain at the top of the forest: turn back, there is nothing to see from the summit.

points.name: Ahu Akivi
points.note: The only inland ahu, its seven moai facing the sea. The trail leaves east along the track past the forest.

points.name: Terevaka summit
points.note: 507 m, the highest point of the island: Rano Kau, Poike and the coast all round. About 1.5 h up, 1 h down.
